deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 study of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane. Here he works on local and combinatorial bookkeeping of such arrangements.

(1) The large figure models RP^2 as a disc whose boundary oval has antipodal identification. Two distinguished pseudolines, D (green, dashed) and D' (yellow-green), run between the two marked boundary points. These two points are one and the same intersection point of D and D' once the boundary is identified. The curled arrows marked 1, 2 at both ends record that passing through the boundary interchanges the two sides/strands, a half-twist. Since RP^2 minus two lines is two open discs, D and D' bound a lens-shaped region. The orange pseudolines cross this region. A dashed brown polygonal path joins the vertices of the arrangement lying in or on the region, ordered along it.

(2) The bottom figure abstracts this region as the 'fuseau de croisement' (crossing lune/spindle). Its two boundary arcs (green and yellow) meet at the two ends, which are the same crossing seen twice. Each other pseudoline enters through one arc and leaves through the other. Inside, pairs of such lines either cross (X) or do not (|). The vertices inside lie on the dashed path, and the crossings bunch up toward the right end. This is essentially the lune between two lines of an arrangement, the object behind Ringel's triangle flips and Goodman-Pollack sweeps/allowable sequences.

(3) The top-right sketch is the same lune with strand labels 1-5 and markings '2:5'. It looks like an attempt to record the order in which the other lines meet the two boundary arcs; the left/right labels may record how this order is permuted from one end to the other.

(4) The middle-right sketch is a vertex where several pseudolines meet (a point of 'spécialité' ≥ 2, i.e. at least two lines pass through it). One line through it is distinguished, and two markers labelled 1 and 2 (green and yellow circles) sit on it, with arrows. This visualises a local frame: a vertex, a line through it, an orientation, and a choice of side.

(5) The text reads roughly as follows.
- 'σ_2 = change of the orientation of D'.
- 'σ_0 = ?'.
- 'The frames (repères) ... corresponding to D-oriented p.r. (points of speciality ≥ 2), equipped moreover with a vertex and an orientation at a vertex, or a sighting (visée) of the complement D(s)?'

So Grothendieck is trying to define a set of 'flags' (repères) of a pseudoline arrangement, carrying a group action by involutions σ_0, σ_1, σ_2, σ. The next page draws a graph of the pairs (σ_i, σ_j), which looks like a Coxeter-type relation diagram. This is the analogue, for pseudoline arrangements, of his cartographic group acting on the flags (vertex, edge, face) of a map in Esquisse d'un programme. The aim is presumably a purely group-theoretic, flag-based encoding of the combinatorial type of an arrangement, with the lune as the basic local configuration.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted, so nothing can be outright wrong. The definition of the frames is explicitly tentative: it ends with a question mark, and σ_0 is left as '?'. The abstract lune drawing does not show how a line can cross the same boundary arc twice; for a pseudoline it cannot, since it meets D and D' once each, and the drawing is consistent with that.

ideas.what: Lune (fuseau) bounded by two pseudolines between their crossing, traversed by the other lines, as the basic local configuration of an arrangement
ideas.modern_name: lune/digon of two lines in an arrangement; local sequences, allowable sequences, triangle flips
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flips); Goodman-Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Felsner and others (wiring diagrams)

ideas.what: Disc model of RP^2 with antipodal boundary identification, showing the half-twist of strands at the identified crossing
ideas.modern_name: standard disc/wiring model of projective pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Flags ('repères') of an arrangement (oriented line, vertex of speciality ≥2, orientation at the vertex or a choice of side), acted on by involutions σ_0, σ_1, σ_2, σ; σ_2 = reversal of the orientation of D
ideas.modern_name: flag systems / cartographic-group-type encoding of maps; flag graphs of arrangements; combinatorial encoding of rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (cartographic group for maps, Esquisse 1984); Jones-Singerman; flag-based descriptions of arrangements via oriented matroids (Folkman-Lawrence 1978, Björner et al.)
ideas.where_published: The cartographic group for maps is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the version for pseudoline arrangements is not known to be published

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to extend his cartographic-group formalism (flags with involutions σ_0, σ_1, σ_2) from maps to pseudoline arrangements. He enriches flags with an oriented line, a vertex on it, and either an orientation at the vertex or a choice of side of D. The intended group, with an extra generator σ, is left undefined (σ_0 = ?).
missed.quote: σ_2 = échange de l'orientation de D ... σ_0 = ? ... les repères ... correspondant aux p.r. D orientées (qui sont de spécialité ≥ 2), munis de plus d'un sommet et d'une orientation en un sommet ou d'une visée du complémentaire D(s)?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rank-3 oriented matroids and pseudoline arrangements are usually encoded by chirotopes, allowable sequences or wiring diagrams. A 'line-aware' cartographic group, finer than the plain map group of the arrangement's cell decomposition, would give a group-theoretic or monodromy-like description of arrangements. It might connect them to Grothendieck's dessins/Teichmüller-tower programme, a link that is little explored.

deep.surprise_reason: The drawings are standard pictures of lunes and the disc model of RP^2. The only notable element is the tentative transplant of the cartographic-group (flag/involution) formalism to pseudoline arrangements. It is interesting as an unfinished thread linking the Esquisse to arrangement combinatorics, but it is undeveloped on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'les repères de la [?] fuseau' is more likely 'les repères de la surface' ('fuseau' is masculine); the word is uncertain.
Last line: 'ou d'une visée du complémentaire D(s)?' fits the image; the opening of that line reads 'en un sommet ou'.
Top-right labels: the right end reads '1↔5' (or '1:5') above and '2:5' below, not just '2:5'.
'p.r.' is unexpanded in the manuscript; from context it means points of the arrangement ('points ... de spécialité ≥ 2'), possibly 'points réels/remarquables'.
